intro.title: Build i18n translation helper with interpolation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple internationalization (i18n) translation helper function that can translate text and insert dynamic values. You'll learn how to use string interpolation to replace placeholders in translation strings with actual data. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, template literals, and object lookups. This project will help you understand how to manage multilingual content in applications. By the end, you'll have a reusable helper that can handle basic translation needs.
intro.usecase: Internationalization (i18n) translation helpers with interpolation are essential in any application serving global users. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, where product descriptions, pricing, and checkout messages need to display in the user's language with dynamic values like product names or dates. In SaaS dashboards like Slack or Notion, interface elements—menus, tooltips, error messages—use interpolation to insert user-specific data (e.g., "You have 3 unread messages") while maintaining consistent translations. This approach ensures your UI adapts seamlessly across languages without hardcoding text, making your app accessible and professional worldwide.
